title: Sabah Half Marathon 2026 Review: Starting at a 35,000-Seat Stadium
seo_title: Sabah Half Marathon 2026 Review | Kota Kinabalu
meta_description: Sabah Half Marathon 2026 review: December 13 at Likas Stadium, Kota Kinabalu -- a 35,000-capacity venue and home of Sabah FC since 1983.
dek: Set for 13 December 2026, this JomRun-organised race starts at Likas Stadium -- Sabah's 35,000-seat multi-purpose venue, home to Sabah FC since 1983 and Malaysia's 8th-largest football stadium.
verdict: The Sabah Half Marathon starts at Likas Stadium, a genuinely major sports venue by regional standards -- 35,000 capacity, home to Sabah FC since 1983, and the 8th-largest football stadium in all of Malaysia. That gives the race real staging capacity and infrastructure, distinct from the mall- or square-anchored venues used by most races in this research batch. Three distances (5K/10K/21.1K), organised via JomRun -- the same organiser behind the KL Half Marathon, Tebrau City Half Marathon and Terengganu Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research -- give this East Malaysia race a familiar, tested framework.

sections.heading: Starting at a Major Football Stadium
paragraphs: The Sabah Half Marathon offers three distances -- 5K, 10K and 21.1K -- starting at Likas Stadium, Kota Kinabalu. [1] Likas Stadium is a multi-purpose venue with a 35,000-seat capacity, mainly used for football and athletics within the broader Likas Sports Complex. [2] It's been the home stadium of Sabah FC since its opening in 1983, renovated in 2001 and again in 2023 for AFC-standard usage, and ranks as the 8th-largest football stadium in Malaysia.

sections.heading: Genuine Athletic Infrastructure
paragraphs: Beyond football, Likas Stadium also serves as home venue for the Sabah FA Women's Team, hosting Malaysia National Women's League and AFC Women's Champions League matches. [2] That dual football/athletics use makes it a genuinely purpose-suited venue for a road race start/finish, with real crowd-handling and staging capacity built in.

sections.heading: A Familiar JomRun Framework
paragraphs: This event is organised via JomRun, the same organiser behind the KL Half Marathon, Tebrau City Half Marathon and Terengganu Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research batch. [1] That gives East Malaysia's Kota Kinabalu the benefit of a tested registration and race-day structure already proven across multiple Peninsular Malaysia events.

sections.heading: A Tight Registration Deadline
paragraphs: Registration is open but closes 12 December 2026 -- the day before race day, matching the tight-window pattern seen at other JomRun-organised events like the KL Half Marathon and Mercedes BR Jaya Half Marathon Duathlon covered elsewhere in this research. [1] Register well ahead rather than waiting.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If a well-organised half marathon starting at a genuinely major stadium venue in East Malaysia appeals, the Sabah Half Marathon on 13 December 2026 is a strong pick. Register before the 12 December deadline, given JomRun's consistently tight registration windows.
